items.title: Generative Modeling of Networked Time-Series via Transformer Architectures
items.raw_content:
Authors: Yusuf Elnady

Many security and network applications require having large datasets to train the machine learning models. Limited data access is a well-known problem in the security domain. Recent studies have shown the potential of Transformer models to enlarge the size of data by synthesizing new samples, but the synthesized samples don't improve the models over the real data. To address this issue, we design an efficient transformer-based model as a generative framework to generate time-series data, that can be used to boost the performance of existing and new ML workflows. Our new transformer model achieves the SOTA results. We style our model to be generalizable and work across different datasets, and produce high-quality samples.
items.title_zh: 基于 Transformer 架构的网络化时间序列生成建模
items.summary: The author designs an efficient transformer-based generative framework for time-series data, motivated by limited data access in security and network applications. The model is reported to reach state-of-the-art results and to generalize across datasets.

items.title: Autonomous drone defeats human champions in racing first
items.raw_content: A team of scientists and students from TU Delft has taken first place at the A2RL Drone Championship in Abu Dhabi - an international race that pushes the limits of physical artificial intelligence, challenging teams to fly fully autonomous drones using only a single camera. The TU Delft drone competed against 13 autonomous drones and even human drone racing champions, using innovative methods to train deep neural networks for high-performance control. The gained knowledge on highly-efficient robust AI will contribute to many robotics applications, from self-driving cars to humanoid robots. For the first time, a drone has beaten human pilots in an international drone racing competition, marking a new milestone in the development of artificial intelligence. On Saturday April 14, 2025, two drone racing events took place simultaneously: The Falcon Cup Finals for human pilots and the A2RL Dro
items.title_zh: 自主无人机在国际竞速赛中首次击败人类冠军
items.summary: A team from TU Delft won the A2RL Drone Championship in Abu Dhabi with a fully autonomous drone that relied on a single camera, competing against 13 autonomous drones and human racing champions. The university says it is the first time a drone has beaten human pilots in an international drone racing competition.

items.title: Paged Attention Meets FlexAttention: Unlocking Long-Context Efficiency in Deployed Inference
items.title_zh: PagedAttention 遇上 FlexAttention：释放长上下文推理效率
items.summary: Researchers integrate PagedAttention with PyTorch's FlexAttention inside IBM's Foundation Model Stack to address fragmentation and inefficiency in monolithic KV-cache allocations. On an NVIDIA L4 GPU, latency grows only linearly from 128 to 2048 tokens, and the implementation is open-sourced.

items.title: A Data-Based Architecture for Flight Test without Test Points
items.title_zh: 一种无需测试点的飞行试验数据驱动架构
items.summary: The authors propose replacing fixed flight-test points with a reduced-order model built from a high-fidelity digital model and updated through Gaussian Process Regression using whatever conditions the pilot actually flies. They demonstrate the approach on T-38C longitudinal data for MIL-STD-1797B compliance assessment.

items.title: FALO: Fast and Accurate LiDAR 3D Object Detection on Resource-Constrained Devices
items.title_zh: FALO：资源受限设备上的快速高精度 LiDAR 3D 目标检测
items.summary: FALO is a hardware-friendly LiDAR 3D object detection method that arranges sparse voxels into a one-dimensional sequence and processes them with ConvDotMix blocks combining large-kernel convolutions, Hadamard products and linear layers. On nuScenes and Waymo it reports competitive accuracy while running 1.6 to 9.8 times faster than the latest state of the art on mobile GPUs and NPUs.

items.title: Securing Traffic Sign Recognition Systems in Autonomous Vehicles
items.title_zh: 保障自动驾驶车辆交通标志识别系统的安全
items.summary: The paper examines error-minimizing poisoning attacks on traffic-sign recognition DNNs and proposes data augmentation-based training; attacks cut accuracy from 99.90% to 10.6%, while the mitigation restored it to 96.05%.

items.title: Subjectivity in the Annotation of Bridging Anaphora
items.title_zh: 桥接回指标注中的主观性
items.summary: The authors study subjectivity in annotating bridging anaphora at three levels, namely anaphor recognition, antecedent resolution and subtype selection, through a pilot on the GUM corpus test set. They propose a new subtype classification system and find that some earlier resources may be severely under-annotated.

items.title: Absorb and Converge: Provable Convergence Guarantee for Absorbing Discrete Diffusion Models
items.title_zh: 吸收与收敛：吸收型离散扩散模型的可证明收敛保证
items.summary: The paper provides the first finite-time error bounds and convergence-rate analysis for discrete diffusion models that use absorbing rate matrices, covering tau-leaping and uniformization samplers. Under suitable assumptions it also gives convergence guarantees without early stopping.

items.title: DiscoSum: Discourse-aware News Summarization
items.title_zh: DiscoSum：篇章感知的新闻摘要
items.summary: The authors introduce a news discourse schema and DiscoSum, a beam-search algorithm for structure-aware summarization that adapts news stories to different social-media styles. Human and automatic evaluations show the approach maintains narrative fidelity and meets structural requirements.
